(repeated).sql: select "a"."attname" as "column", "a"."attnotnull" as "not_null", "a"."atthasdef" as "has_default", "c"."relname" as "table", "c"."relkind" as "table_type", "ns"."nspname" as "schema", "typ"."typname" as "type", "dtns"."nspname" as "type_schema", col_description(a.attrelid, a.attnum) as "column_description", pg_get_serial_sequence(quote_ident(ns.nspname) || '.' || quote_ident(c.relname), a.attname) as "auto_incrementing" from "pg_catalog"."pg_attribute" as "a" inner join "pg_catalog"."pg_class" as "c" on "a"."attrelid" = "c"."oid" inner join "pg_catalog"."pg_namespace" as "ns" on "c"."relnamespace" = "ns"."oid" inner join "pg_catalog"."pg_type" as "typ" on "a"."atttypid" = "typ"."oid" inner join "pg_catalog"."pg_namespace" as "dtns" on "typ"."typnamespace" = "dtns"."oid" where "c"."relkind" in ($1, $2, $3, $4) and "ns"."nspname" !~ $5 and "ns"."nspname" != $6 and "ns"."nspname" != $7 and has_schema_privilege(ns.nspname, 'USAGE') and "a"."attnum" >= $8 and "a"."attisdropped" != $9 and "c"."relname" != $10 and "c"."relname" != $11 order by "ns"."nspname", "c"."relname", "a"."attnum"

SELECT
					table_class.relname AS "tableName",
					index_class.relname AS "indexName",
					index_attribute.attname AS "columnName",
					index_data.indisunique AS "isUnique",
					index_data.indisvalid AS "isValid",
					(index_data.indpred IS NOT NULL) AS "isPartial",
					index_column.ordinality AS "columnPosition"
				FROM pg_class AS table_class
				INNER JOIN pg_namespace AS table_namespace
					ON table_namespace.oid = table_class.relnamespace
				INNER JOIN pg_index AS index_data
					ON index_data.indrelid = table_class.oid
				INNER JOIN pg_class AS index_class
					ON index_class.oid = index_data.indexrelid
				INNER JOIN LATERAL unnest(index_data.indkey)
					WITH ORDINALITY AS index_column(attribute_number, ordinality)
					ON TRUE
				LEFT JOIN pg_attribute AS index_attribute
					ON index_attribute.attrelid = table_class.oid
					AND index_attribute.attnum = index_column.attribute_number
				WHERE table_namespace.nspname = $1
					AND table_class.relkind = 'r'
					AND index_column.ordinality <= index_data.indnkeyatts

signs Supabase's users in with their own.sql:
-- The columns Better Auth needs on Supabase's auth.users, written by `protobase import supabase`.
-- Empty until the import's accounts migration fills them from what Supabase recorded; NULL where it recorded nothing.
alter table auth.users
  add column name text,
  add column email_verified boolean,
  add column image text,
  add column app_role text,
  add column banned boolean,
  add column ban_reason text,
  add column ban_expires timestamptz;

-- The value GoTrue writes into every user it makes, for the triggers and policies that read it on new sign-ups.
alter table auth.users alter column role set default 'authenticated', alter column aud set default 'authenticated';
SELECT pg_catalog.current_schemas(true)::text[] AS schemas
select "nspname" from "pg_catalog"."pg_namespace"
select "nspname" from "pg_catalog"."pg_namespace"

-- Supabase's users signing in with Better Auth, written by `protobase import supabase` once their rows were loaded.

-- The user columns, from what Supabase Auth recorded. A ban lasts until banned_until, as on Supabase: Better Auth lifts
-- it once ban_expires has passed.
update auth.users set
  name = coalesce(raw_user_meta_data->>'full_name', raw_user_meta_data->>'name'),
  email_verified = email_confirmed_at is not null,
  image = coalesce(raw_user_meta_data->>'avatar_url', raw_user_meta_data->>'picture'),
  banned = case when banned_until is not null then true end,
  ban_expires = banned_until;

-- Each password, as Supabase hashed it: Better Auth verifies the bcrypt hash and stores it again as its own on sign-in.
-- Only for confirmed addresses: GoTrue refuses a password sign-in to an unconfirmed one and Better Auth would not, so
-- whoever signed up with someone else's address could sign in as them. Those users sign in by code or reset a password.
insert into auth.account (account_id, provider_id, user_id, password, created_at, updated_at)
select id::text, 'credential', id, encrypted_password, coalesce(created_at, now()), coalesce(updated_at, now())
from auth.users where encrypted_password is not null and encrypted_password <> '' and email_confirmed_at is not null;

-- Each identity of a social provider, by Better Auth's name for it and the claim it keys the account on. Sessions and
-- provider tokens stay behind: everyone signs in once. Only for users with a confirmed address or none, for the reason
-- above: GoTrue refuses a provider sign-in to an unconfirmed one too, though it keeps the identity.
insert into auth.account (account_id, provider_id, user_id, created_at, updated_at)
select account_id, provider_id, user_id, created_at, updated_at from (
  select case provider when 'azure' then identity_data->'custom_claims'->>'oid' else provider_id end as account_id, case provider when 'azure' then 'microsoft' when 'linkedin_oidc' then 'linkedin' when 'slack_oidc' then 'slack' when 'x' then 'twitter' else provider end as provider_id, user_id, coalesce(created_at, now()) as created_at, coalesce(updated_at, now()) as updated_at
  from auth.identities where provider <> all(array['email', 'phone', 'anonymous']) and provider not like 'sso:%' and user_id in (select id from auth.users where email is null or email_confirmed_at is not null)
) identity where account_id is not null;
select email, name, email_verified, image, banned, ban_expires = banned_until as ban_kept, app_role from auth.users order by email
select u.email, a.provider_id, a.account_id = u.id::text as own_id, a.account_id, left(a.password, 4) as hash from auth.account a join auth.users u on u.id = a.user_id order by 1, 2
SELECT pg_catalog.current_schemas(true)::text[] AS schemas
